We need to be mindful to avoid overgeneralizations that can come with the consumerization of health care and guide the development and implementation of digital health solutions so we avoid developing new health care deserts. results.title: The beneficial workplace - Mercer
results.content: Emily Ferreira speaks with Mercer’s Director of Research for Health and Benefits, Beth Umland, about what is contributing to the highest healthcare cost growth in 15 years and how employers are responding. Listen as Emily Ferreira speaks with Chief Health Actuary Sunit Patel on Mercer’s preliminary projection for 2026 health benefit cost growth - and what employers can do about it. In the latest installment of the Beneficial Workplace podcast, host Emily Ferreira sits down with Kate Brown, leader of Mercer’s Center for Health Innovation, to discuss how AI is currently integrated into health benefit programs, the increasing usage of agentic AI in benefits administration and how AI will continue to evolve within the healthcare sphere in the years to come. For the full webinar, [click here](https://www.mercer.com/en-us/insights/events/breakthrough-strategies-to-slow-health-cost-growth/). Host Emily Ferreira speaks with inclusive benefits specialist Lindsay Bower on Mercer survey data in the area of women’s health and how employers are addressing their needs today, where gaps remain and what we see for future offerings.

results.title: Lee M. Sanders, MD, MPH - Stanford Profiles
results.content: To assess the health literacy and numeracy skills of Spanish-speaking parents of young children and to validate a new Spanish language health literacy assessment for parents, the Spanish Parental Health Literacy Activities Test (PHLAT Spanish).Cross-sectional study of Spanish-speaking caregivers of young children (<30 months) enrolled at primary care clinics in 4 academic medical centers. To assess parental health literacy and numeracy skills in understanding instructions for caring for young children, and to develop and validate a new parental health literacy scale, the Parental Health Literacy Activities Test (PHLAT).Caregivers of infants (age <13 months) were recruited in a cross-sectional study at pediatric clinics at 3 academic medical centers. The purpose of this work was to assess the association between caregiver health literacy and the use and cost of child health services.We conducted a cross-sectional study of caregiver-child dyads from a sample of children aged 12 months to 12 years presenting to the pediatric emergency department of an urban, public hospital.
